note: Hand-written words and starting topics for the Explore preview. Each is a plain, checkable fact. Real geography only: no dummy subject data (Owner, 2026-11-13). 'Who found it?' (continents, oceans; Owner's yes 2026-11-13): the first people to reach or cross it, not a later arrival from far away, with dates hedged to what is widely agreed. A who-answer must belong to that one topic: an answer shared by several (early humans for Africa, Asia and Europe) says nothing, so the topic gets no 'Who found it?' at all (Owner, 2026-11-13).

points.name: Singapore
points.line: An island city and country at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula.

points.name: First Peoples of Australia
points.line: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, whose ancestors reached Australia at least 50,000 years ago.

points.name: Norse sailors
points.line: Seafarers from Scandinavia, sometimes called Vikings. About 1,000 years ago they sailed to Iceland, Greenland and North America.

points.name: Arctic peoples
points.line: The Inuit and the peoples before them, who have lived on the coasts and sea ice of the far north for thousands of years.

points.name: James Cook
points.line: A British sea captain and map-maker of the 1700s who sailed the Pacific and the far south.

points.name: Fabian von Bellingshausen
points.line: A sea captain who led a Russian voyage round Antarctica in 1819 to 1821.

points.name: Edward Bransfield
points.line: A British naval officer who charted part of the Antarctic Peninsula in 1820.
